title: Birth in 1887 and father's harmonica
summary: Mello was born in 1887 near the interview house; no relatives were professional musicians, but his father played harmonica tunes like Swanee River.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And the first thing we usually like to ask people is the date and place of their birth.
Right here in the Walls, two blocks away from here, 1887. On Betholome? On Betholome in Ibogunny. And the exact date of your birth? June the 4th.
On what year? 1887. 1887. Next. And did any of your family play music in your father's generation? None of them. Played a harmonica.

Your father? No. Just around the house. He never played. Not professional, amateur, semi-professional. He just played. Now they used to play harmonica. That is home for the kids, you know? Next. And your grandfather? None. Nobody. Mm-hmm. Nobody back in that generation? Not nobody in the first generation.
Do you remember any of the tunes your father played on the harmonica?

Oh, yeah. All them old tunes. Swanee River. And I only just wanted to know. Widow done. Six Little Angels. Boy, we're going back now. We're going back now. We used to play that Long Sonata. Oh, yeah? Yeah, Long Sonata used to, because you see, he knew it. And I knew it. And when we played, we had with Jack Lane, Jack Lane to make all kind of four faces. Man, he'd be making faces a day, you know, and Mark McCurt sitting on the side of me. He'd be laughing or just Long Sonata, guitar and the string bass player that kept the music, kept the melody out. We used to play all that old-time stuff. And it used to go. It used to go. This stuff that they play now, what they call jazz, that's as far away from jazz as the moon is from the city of New Orleans. I'm going to tell you what I know. Next, go ahead. Question.
